question: Which field represents "escalated" in this org (the standard Case.IsEscalated checkbox, a custom field, or a Status value), and if a Case is escalated, un-escalated, and later re-escalated, should each new escalation send a fresh email or only the very first one ever?
why: Decides the flow's trigger field and doesRequireRecordChangedToMeetCriteria; the wrong field misses real escalations, and the wrong transition-vs-repeat answer either sends nothing on a repeat escalation or spams the owner on every unrelated edit.
proposed_default: Standard Case.IsEscalated checkbox. Every new transition into true (including a repeat escalation after being un-escalated) sends a fresh email, since each represents a new unhappy-customer event; edits that leave IsEscalated unchanged never re-fire it.
answer_shape: The field API name, plus a yes/no on whether repeat escalations re-notify.

question: Who should the notification email appear to come from, and does anyone need to monitor replies to that address?
why: Sender identity is an org-wide email address that must exist and be verified in the target org before the flow can send from it.
proposed_default: Send from the org's default Organization-Wide Email Address (fall back to the flow's running-user context if none is configured). No reply monitoring is needed — the Account Owner is expected to open the Case in Salesforce rather than reply by email.
answer_shape: A named Organization-Wide Email Address (or explicit decision not to use one) and whether replies need a monitored mailbox.

question: What should happen if the Case has no related Account, or the Account has no Owner (or the owner is a Queue rather than a person)? Who, if anyone, should be notified instead?
why: "Make it automatic" hides the exception path; without a decision, a null Account or Owner either silently drops the alert or fails invisibly inside the flow's own error email.
proposed_default: If the Case has no related Account, skip the email and log the skip. If the Account Owner is a Queue rather than a User, send to the queue's email address if one exists; otherwise fall back to notifying the Support Manager / Case-escalation admin distribution list. No customer-facing failure either way.
answer_shape: A named decision and fallback recipient for each of the two null/edge cases.

question: If the Get-Account-Owner or Send-Email step fails (bad address, deleted user, etc.), who should find out, and how?
why: Without a fault path the interview stops and the error is invisible outside the flow's own error email, which nobody but the running user ever sees.
proposed_default: The fault path writes an entry using the repo's standard flow-fault logging pattern (Application_Log__c, per templates/flow/FaultPath_Template.md) and emails the Salesforce admin distribution list. No customer-facing impact.
answer_shape: Confirmation of the fault-logging target and who is on the admin distribution list.

question: Does this change touch only fields on the Case being saved, or does it also need to read the related Account/Owner and send email?
why: Same-record-only work fits a before-save flow; anything that sends email or reads a related object forces after-save.
proposed_default: After-save — the flow reads the related Account's Owner and sends email, neither of which a before-save flow can do (confirmed by standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md Q2/Q4/Q5).
answer_shape: Confirmation of RecordAfterSave as the trigger type.

question: What else already runs on Case in the after-save context, and does this new flow need to run before or after any of it?
why: Two flows in one save context with no declared order is undefined sequencing.
proposed_default: No other after-save automation is known to depend on ordering relative to this notification; run at the default triggerOrder. This flow never writes back to the Case, so it cannot conflict with another flow's field ownership.
answer_shape: A triggerOrder value, or confirmation none is needed.

question: Does anything downstream update this Case again as a result of this flow, creating a recursion risk?
why: An after-save flow that re-saves its own object re-enters the save procedure and can behave differently on the second pass.
proposed_default: No — this flow only sends an email and never performs DML on the Case or Account, so there is no recursion risk and no recursion guard is needed.
answer_shape: Confirmation the flow performs no DML, or a recursion-guard design if it does.

question: Should the email send immediately when the Case is escalated, or can/should it be delayed (e.g., batched, or gated to business hours)?
why: A delayed notification needs a FlowScheduledPath; an immediate one does not.
proposed_default: Immediate — send synchronously in the same after-save transaction. Do not gate on business hours; an unhappy customer alert loses its value if it waits for morning.
answer_shape: Immediate vs. a named delay/business-hours gate.

question: When a Case of this kind is deleted, does anything about this notification need to be preserved or cleaned up?
why: RecordBeforeDelete is the only delete context that exists for record-triggered flows, and there is no after-delete equivalent.
proposed_default: Not applicable — this flow only reacts to Case updates (escalation), not deletes; no delete-context flow is needed.
answer_shape: Confirmation no delete-context handling is required.

question: Is the flow's recordTriggerType Create, Update, or CreateAndUpdate — i.e., can a Case ever arrive already escalated on creation?
why: Decides which $Record parameters the FlowTest Start test point may carry; the wrong pair fails deploy.
proposed_default: Update only — Cases are not created pre-escalated in this org; escalation always happens as a later edit to an existing Case.

question: Is this email built as a Flow Send Email action (Flow Text Template resource) or as a classic Email Alert referencing a Classic Email Template invoked from the flow?
why: Rules deployed by metadata (assignment/auto-response/escalation) can only reference Classic templates; a pure Flow build is not bound by that constraint and can use either mechanism.
proposed_default: Flow Send Email action with a Flow Text Template resource — simplest for a two-merge-field, internal-only notification with no reuse across other automations.
answer_shape: Send Email action + Text Template, or Email Alert + Classic Template — with a reason if the latter.

question: Which record is the merge context (Case, with the Account reached via relationship), and beyond the Case Number and Subject the requirement names, should anything else appear in the email (a link to the record, the Account name, who escalated it)?
why: Merge fields resolve only for the firing record and its parents; scoping the merge context up front avoids templates that render blanks.
proposed_default: Merge context is Case, reaching Account.Owner via the Case→Account relationship. Beyond Case Number and Subject, include a direct link to the Case record and the Account Name, since a bare case number/subject still leaves the Account Owner needing to open the record.
answer_shape: The merge field list, confirmed against what the requirement explicitly asked for.

question: Does this email depend on an Email-to-Case thread reference token?
why: Removing a thread reference from a customer-facing case email breaks reply threading.
proposed_default: Not applicable — this is an internal notification to the Account Owner, not a customer-facing Case communication, so no Email-to-Case threading token is involved.

question: Walk me through what happens today, right now, when a Case gets escalated — is there any existing manual step (a phone call, a Slack ping, a manual email) this notification is meant to replace?
why: Stakeholders sometimes describe a workaround built around a gap as if it were the whole requirement; missing it produces a to-be design that duplicates rather than replaces the workaround.
proposed_default: No existing automated notification exists; this is net-new automation. Any manual heads-up an agent currently gives (a call, a Slack ping) may continue in parallel — this flow does not need to replace it, only to guarantee the Account Owner always gets one.
answer_shape: An as-is step list, if a workaround exists.

question: Does anyone need record- or field-level access changed to support this (e.g., a profile that currently cannot see Account.Owner)?
why: Record access and field access are different mechanisms in different places; automation running in system context can silently mask a visibility gap a human would hit.
proposed_default: No sharing or field-level-security changes are needed. The flow runs in automation/system context and only reads Case/Account/Owner to build the email; it does not grant or need any new user-facing visibility.
answer_shape: A sharing_impact value naming a layer, or "none."

question: Roughly how many Cases get escalated per day (steady state and worst case), to confirm this stays well under the org's mass-email and Flow governor limits?
why: Automation that passes UAT on ten records can fail at volume; the transaction limits are shared by Flow and Apex.
proposed_default: Escalations are a small fraction of total daily Case volume (single digits to low tens per day in a typical support org of this shape) — far under the ~1,000/day mass-email cap and well within a single-record after-save flow's per-transaction limits, since each escalation fires its own transaction rather than a bulk batch.
answer_shape: A steady-state number and a worst-case single-day number.

question: Does any of this data live outside Salesforce (e.g., is "escalated" status or Account ownership synced in from another system)?
why: A requirement sourced from another system is an integration requirement wearing an automation costume, and needs a pattern decision before sizing.
proposed_default: No — Case, Account, and Owner all live natively in Salesforce; no external system or integration is involved in this notification.
answer_shape: Confirmation of no integration, or a named source system.

question: Is the Account Owner always an internal Salesforce employee user, or could it be a partner/customer-community user?
why: The answer selects a licence, and licence selects API allocation and portal template long before design starts.
proposed_default: Account Owners are internal Salesforce employee users (standard Salesforce licence); no customer or partner community licence implication.

question: Is there a reporting need behind this (e.g., a dashboard of escalation notifications sent), or is the email itself the entire deliverable?
why: Reporting requirements assume joins the report-type rules may forbid; scoping this now avoids a same-week follow-up request treated as in-scope.
proposed_default: No reporting requirement — the email itself is the entire deliverable for this ask. A future report on escalated Cases and notification history is out of scope here and can be requested separately.
answer_shape: Confirmation of no reporting need, or a named reporting row.
